It is one of the candidate shrines for "Ama-no-Iwato-wake-Yakura-hime Shrine," the {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}} and {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}}<ref>Other candidate shrines are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yakura-hime Shrine}} and {{ill|Kamiichinomiya Ōawa Shrine|ja|上一宮大粟神社|zh|上一宮大粟神社|qid=Q11358379}}.</ref>. Under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}}, it was a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. It is selected as a {{ill|Tokushima Civic Heritage|ja|とくしま市民遺産|qid=Q11273094}} site. {{nihongo|'''Ichinomiya Shrine'''|一宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== Overview ==
It enshrines {{ill|Ōgetsuhime|Q3261482|qid=Q3261482|lt=Ōgetsu-hime-no-Mikoto}} and Ama-no-Iwato-wake-Yakura-hime-no-Mikoto.

The shrine is in western Tokushima City, and the surrounding area is called "Ichinomiya-chō." On the summit of the mountain to the east once stood {{ill|Ichinomiya Castle|Q11266820|qid=Q11266820|lt=Ichinomiya Castle}} of the {{ill|Ogasawara clan|Q2975340|qid=Q2975340}}. Originally, {{ill|Kamiichinomiya Ōawa Shrine|ja|上一宮大粟神社|zh|上一宮大粟神社|qid=Q11358379}} (in {{ill|Myōzai District, Tokushima|Q1155732|qid=Q1155732}}, {{ill|Kamiyama, Tokushima|Q1350922|qid=Q1350922}}) was the ichinomiya of Awa Province, but because worship there was inconvenient, it is said that a branch shrine was established near the provincial office in the late Heian period, and this shrine became the ichinomiya.

Later, because Ichinomiya Castle stood nearby, the area including this shrine became a main battleground during the Tenshō campaigns of the Sengoku period and was burned over. In the early Edo period, however, the third lord of Awa Domain, Hachisuka Mitsutaka, quickly restored it, and by 1653 the pilgrim Sūzen wrote in his book that "the haiden is three bays to each side and the halls are splendidly built."

Across the road in front of the shrine stands {{ill|Dainichi-ji (Tokushima)|Q11435622|qid=Q11435622|lt=Dainichi-ji}}, Temple No. 13 of the {{ill|Shikoku Pilgrimage|Q1972399|qid=Q1972399}}. Before the early Meiji separation of Shinto and Buddhism, this shrine itself was the pilgrimage site, while Dainichi-ji was the bettō temple and served as the nōkyō office. There are also traces that nōkyō entries were made here under "Ichinomiya Daimyōjin, honji-butsu Jūichimen Kannon, Daigūji." After the early Meiji separation, the shrine's honji image of Jūichimen Kannon was moved to Dainichi-ji's main hall as principal image, the pilgrimage site was transferred, and the bettō relationship ended.

== Precincts ==
* Honden and haiden
* Precinct shrines (hokora)
** Wakaba Shrine: enshrines the heroic spirits of 238 war dead.
** Sarutahiko Shrine
** Tenjin Shrine
** Ōnamuchi Shrine and Kotoshironushi Shrine
** Munakata Shrine
** Wakamiya Shrine: enshrines successive castle lords.
** Shūsai Shrine: a shrine where parishioners gather and converse

== Cultural properties ==
[[File:Ichinomiya Shrine 22 July 2023 2.jpg|thumb|Honden]]
; Important Cultural Property (national designation)
* Honden (with 9 munafuda plaques) - built in Kan'ei 7 (1630). Three-bay nagare-zukuri with front chidori-hafu, copper-sheet roofing. The one-bay kōhai is in karahafu style, with richly colored carvings at key points. Designated 1993-04-20.
